title: Exploring the Pathway and Therapeutic Management of Synchronous K601E BRAF-Mutated Gastric Adenocarcinoma and Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report
content: BRAF mutations are mostly detected in melanoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. In gastric cancer, BRAF mutations are rare, and there is no information available on the specific K601EBRAF mutation in this field. In this report, we present a clinical case of a 50-year-old female patient with synchronous primary extensive small cell lung cancer and metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma with K601EBRAF mutation, which has not been described in the literature until now. Although the impact of this mutation on gastric cancer is still unknown, the de-scription of rare clinical cases like this and the approach adopted could be important to increase knowledge about it in the scientific community.
